match_id: JAISSLE: “I COULD GET IN TROUBLE!”  Newcastle_Liverpool ⚽ Premier League_2026-08-23_Dw5cfDCIISs
team: JAISSLE: “I COULD GET IN TROUBLE!”  Newcastle
quote_text:
Matthias, you must have very mixed  feelings after such a thrilling game.  
First of all, hello everyone. It was  indeed a game with mixed feelings,  
especially in the end when you, yeah, when  you get a decision which took two points  
away. It's hard. It's really hard to digest. But  overall, there's also a lot of confidence and  
somehow we are really proud of what  we saw throughout the 90 minutes.  
The young lads were doing an amazing job with  all the challenges in that transition period.  
I'm not tired of mentioning that because this  was special. They were already delivering on  
a high level and that makes us proud. Did that  performance state everything you want from your  
Newcastle United team? It was already a lot  what we want to see. Therefore, what I said,  
we are really proud in that short amount of  time to see the lads as a unit on the pitch,  
really committed to what they're doing. And  this is a really good base to build on. What  
were your thoughts on the late penalty?  Pardon? Your thoughts on the late penalty.  
I have clear thoughts. Probably you saw that in  my reaction. For me, it's a really soft penalty,  
as you call it here, I guess. So if you give these  penalties, then you need to give a lot throughout  
the match and a lot throughout the season. And I  don't know if this is for the good of football. In  
terms of individual players, you touched on some  of the younger ones. One of the older players,  
Yoane Wissa, had a nightmare first season. Today  he looked like an unrecognisable player from that.  
Can you just talk to us about him and how you've  sort of [inaudible]? Amazing performance. Amazing  
performance. Even though he could have killed  the game, but you know, this is football. When  
I talk about Wissa, it's not just if he scores or  makes an assist. It's about how he's committed,  
how he's working for the teammates. And it's not  only Wissa. There are many, many other lads today  
I can mention. Again, this is the basis. This  should be the fundament for Newcastle United.  
And I mentioned that in the pre-match conference  already, that if you have this synergy between the  
fans and then the players delivering on the pitch,  then something special can be created. Matthias,  
could you give us some insight into what Joe  Willock has been like for you as a player since  
you've been here? There's been a lot of talk about  his future, but today he showed [inaudible]. Yeah,  
it was Joe like we wish to see him, right? He  showed that already in pre-season, in these three  
weeks now, that he has this potential. And today  I'm so happy that he stepped on the pitch when it  
was needed, and he showed that straight away. Pure  commitment again from him. We can go through the  
whole squad today and it's so important, not only  the starting 11 players but also the non-starters,  
that they have that commitment. If they're needed,  if they come in, they deliver. So I'm really  
proud. Is Joe Willock somebody you would like to  keep? Sure. With these performances? Definitely.  
You appointed Dan Burn as your captain for the  season and Joelinton as your vice-captain. You've  
lost them both through injury. Did you see other  leaders emerge today? Sorry, I need to ask again  
because I didn't get it in the end. You were  without your captain and vice-captain, but you  
had other players who looked like real leaders.  Yes. First of all, it's tough if you miss the  
two captains. Hopefully they come back as soon as  possible. But that was what we said also, right?  
Then there's a vacuum where other players need  to step in. And this is amazing. Young lads, you  
know, taking responsibility. Top. Really top. It's  something special for the start. I'm really proud.  
This time last week, Amar Dedić wasn't even a  Newcastle player. What was your message to him  
today before throwing him into such a big game?  Obviously, he played well as well. The good part  
was that he knew our identity. He knew already  beforehand how we want to play football, and he's  
a player fitting to that style. So it was easy for  him to adapt. But also, I have to say, chapeau,  
how fast he adapted then in the Premier League.  Played 90 minutes against a tough opponent. So I'm  
really happy. You spoke in the build-up about your  excitement ahead of the game. I wonder, firstly,  
how you slept last night ahead of the game and,  secondly, how you found that atmosphere today when  
it kicked off. I slept really good, thanks.  But there was excitement as well. And this  
is important also for a coach, for players, that  they're desperate to go on the pitch, to be on the  
sideline. And that was the case today. I couldn't  wait for the start. Then, if you go out through  
the tunnel, special atmosphere. Goosebumps. So I  consider that really as a huge privilege, being  
coach of Newcastle United. We saw plenty of long  balls from Newcastle from deep-lying positions,  
from defence, from Malick Thiaw and Lewis Miley.  Is that evidence of the vertical football you've  
described so far? Just a part of the element.  Football is a complex sport. It's always also  
related to what the opponent is giving you.  And today that was the approach. It can be a  
bit different in the next one. Can I ask about the  injury to Dan Burn? What's the timescale for him,  
please? Also, Will Osula, is that an injury you  think will keep him out for a period? Yeah. With  
Dan, it's clear that he will be out for a couple  of weeks. How long exactly, that will be decided.  
But for sure, our medical department is excellent,  so he will be as fast as possible back again on  
the grass. And with Will, we need to see. It's  hopefully not that serious, that he is back as  
soon as possible as well. For now, it looks  quite good, but we need to see and check him.  
Just on Will, he gives you so much when he plays  up there. You don't really have a like-for-like  
replacement when he's not available. Yoane went  up and did really well, but then you kind of lose  
what Yoane was giving you in his other position.  Is that something you're maybe going to have to  
think about? Because Will seems to be playing a  very specialist role for you. That's right. And  
I thought about that. So we will see. We see seven  days left, I think, approximately. Lewis Miley was  
excellent today. He's a player who, with some  of the players Newcastle lost this summer, I've  
always thought was going to have a big role this  season. How important is he going to be for you,  
and what did you make of his performance? I'm a  big fan. Not putting too much pressure on him,  
but honestly, coming back from a long injury  with a really short pre-season and showing that  
now in the first match is something special.  And I'm just, you know, proud to be a part of  
his development now, because hopefully we  have a player with a really bright future.  
What was your message to the players after the  game? Cannot repeat everything because then I  
could get in trouble and may need to pay some  fines. But overall, I told them that I'm really,  
really proud for what I saw over 90 minutes.  That this is a really, really top starting point,  
a fundament where we can build on this commitment,  you know, this activity in all phases, intensity  
in all phases. We were there for each other. If  something went wrong, we acted really like a unit.  
And this, in such a short amount of time, that's a  top starting point. And the frustration was there  
as well. But these are the challenges we had now  in pre-season with that transition phase. It's  
normal. And today someone, someone, yes, threw  some stones in the way, and we need to take that  
out to be successful again. Matthias, a really  impressive performance from your side today.  
Obviously, it's still early stages. If supporters  were to watch your team at the end of this season,  
what would you be hoping would be different from  what we saw today? It's really nice. Therefore,  
we're also happy, even though we draw in the  end, but we saw already so many good things,  
really. I think the fans, they can identify the  team with, you know, with their expectations,  
the way how we want to play. And this is already  like a high, high standard, and we want to improve  
on that. The players who played today, they  were young, many of them unexperienced in the  
Premier League. So they will improve, they  will adapt even better. So that's the way.
